subject: general
question: According to the Census of India 2011, what was the population growth rate in Kerala?
solution:
The correct answer is __**4.91%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• According to the Census of India 2011, Kerala recorded the lowest population growth rate among all major states in the country.
 
• The decadal population growth rate in Kerala for the period 2001-2011 was 4.91%.
 
• This figure represents a significant decline compared to the population growth rate of 9.43% recorded in the previous decade (1991-2001).
 
• Kerala's consistently low population growth rate is attributed to several factors, including high levels of literacy, particularly among women.
 
• Higher female literacy rates are often correlated with greater awareness and adoption of family planning measures.
 
• The state has also made significant strides in healthcare, leading to lower infant mortality rates and increased life expectancy.
 
• Improved access to and awareness of healthcare services contribute to smaller family sizes.
 
• Social development indicators in Kerala, such as high levels of education and healthcare access, have played a crucial role in influencing fertility rates.
 
• The state has a relatively high age of marriage for both men and women, which also contributes to lower fertility rates.
 
• Out-migration, particularly of males seeking employment in other parts of India and abroad, has also influenced the population growth rate.
 
• While out-migration doesn't directly reduce the birth rate, it can affect the overall population increase within the state.
 
• The total fertility rate (TFR) in Kerala has been consistently below the replacement level for several decades.
 
• The replacement level fertility rate is generally considered to be 2.1 children per woman, the rate at which a population exactly replaces itself from one generation to the next.
